threshold_plan.scope: range, rounded-prefix, cross-boundary set-clear, summary, exact nth-lookup, and copy-behavior checkpoints
threshold_plan.why_not_approved_yet: The live gate is still a bounded rollback-readiness slice, direct `bitmap_fill(..., 115)` still stops at bit 114 in the shipped Zig helper, and no approved benchmark command or acceptable limit has landed for this gate yet.

gaps.why_now: The live Phase 4 gate already replays bounded range, rounded-prefix, cross-boundary set-clear, summary, exact find_nth_bit, and copy-behavior expectations from lib/test_bitmap.c, so the survey should point at that shipped gate instead of inventing a second parallel bitmap diff surface.

This manifest-backed bitmap survey keeps the current rollback evidence gap, shared replay contract, and roadmap destination explicit in one machine-checkable packet instead of leaving the bitmap survey only inside prose and inline comments.

The shared phase4_build.zig entrypoint already keeps `phase4-bitmap-diff-tests` in the rollback-readiness bundle, but it does not yet run a dedicated bitmap survey test or expose an isolated survey step for this new manifest-backed packet.

The validation matrix already names the rollback owner, threshold posture, and current rollback evidence gap for `zigux/tests/bitmap_diff.zig`, so the bitmap survey should point at that published ownership note instead of restating it loosely.

The live gate is still a bounded rollback-readiness slice. It keeps the rounded-fill drift explicit because direct `bitmap_fill(..., 115)` still stops at bit 114 in the shipped Zig helper instead of matching the full lib/test_bitmap.c rounded two-word anchor, and Phase 4 still publishes no approved perf threshold for the broader bitmap surface.
